Ben Affleck's What Company Just Got Bought by Netflix?
Netflix Just Broke Its Own Golden Rule to Buy Ben Affleck’s Secret AI Startup
Netflix Taps Ben Affleck to Help Get More Filmmakers to Use AI
sources.text:
Netflix is teaming up with Ben Affleck and leveraging the goodwill he’s earned with his views on AI to bring even more AI tools into filmmaking.
The streaming giant announced today that it has acquired Affleck’s filmmaking tech company, InterPositive, which the actor quietly founded in 2022 to develop AI-powered tools for filmmakers.
Netflix did not disclose the terms of the acquisition. But Variety reported that InterPositive’s 16-person team will join Netflix, with Affleck serving as a senior adviser. The company reportedly plans to offer InterPositive’s tools to its creative partners rather than selling commercial access to them.
In a press release, Affleck explained his motivation for founding InterPositive. He wrote that after spending time observing the early rise of AI in film production, many of the models fell short. So, he decided to take matters into his own hands.
“Together with a small team of engineers, researchers and creatives, I began filming a proprietary dataset on a controlled soundstage with all the familiarities of a full production,” Affleck said. “I wanted to build a workflow that captures what happens on a set, with vocabulary that matched the language cinematographers and directors already spoke and included the kind of consistency and controls they would expect.”
Affleck said the model was specifically trained to understand “visual logic and editorial consistency.”
In a video accompanying the announcement, Affleck emphasized that the tool is “not about text prompting or generating something from nothing.”
Instead, filmmakers can build their own model using their movie’s footage and then use it in post-production to make changes like removing stunt wires, creating missing shots, or adjusting backdrops, colors, and lighting.
The news is somewhat surprising after Affleck’s past comments expressing a more skeptical view of AI have gon viral. In particular, he has questioned AI’s ability to write, saying that “by its nature it goes to the mean, the average.”
“I don’t think it’s very likely that it’s gonna be able to write anything meaningful, or in particular, that it’s going to be making movies from whole cloth, like Tilly Norwood. That’s bullshit,” Affleck said on The Joe Rogan Podcast in January about AI, referencing the AI-generated actor. “Really, what it is, it’s going to be a tool just like visual effects.”
So it’s no surprise Netflix is tapping Affleck to help get filmmakers on the AI bandwagon.
The company said last year that it plans to expand its use of AI. In a letter to shareholders in October, Netflix wrote that it aims to focus on “empowering creators with a broad set of GenAI tools to help them achieve their visions.”
The company also highlighted some early examples of the technology in action. Netflix touted its use of de-aging AI in Happy Gilmore 2, and said the producers of Billionaires’ Bunker used AI tools to create concept art.
Even before that, Netflix announced in July that the Argentinian sci-fi series El Eternauta featured what the company described as the “very first GenAI final footage to appear on screen” in a Netflix show or film
With this new partnership, it’s pretty safe to assume that we’ll be seeing more AI show up in Netflix productions. Hopefully, Affleck can help prevent it from being too cringe.

sources.news_title: ‘This is a really meaningful innovation’: Netflix buys Ben Affleck’s AI startup - The Boston Globe
sources.text:
It sounds like Ben Affleck has been working on a lot more than just Dunkin’ commercials over the past few years.
Netflix announced on Thursday that it has acquired InterPositive, Affleck’s company that creates AI-powered tools for filmmakers. The news comes after it was revealed earlier this week that Artist Equity, the production company helmed by Affleck and Matt Damon, has entered into a first-look deal with the streaming giant.
According to Netflix’s announcement, the entire InterPositive team will join Netflix, with Affleck also coming along for the ride to serve as a senior advisor. The announcement also included a note from the Cambridge-raised Oscar winner, with Affleck writing that, starting in 2022, he “spent a lot of time observing the early rise of AI in production” and got into the space as he felt he had a “responsibility to my peers and our industry, to protect the power of human creativity and the people behind it.”
“Together with a small team of engineers, researchers, and creatives, I began filming a proprietary dataset on a controlled soundstage with all the familiarities of a full production,” Affleck wrote. “I wanted to build a workflow that captures what happens on a set, with vocabulary that matched the language cinematographers and directors already spoke and included the kind of consistency and controls they would expect.”
FEATURED VIDEO
In a video interview with Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria and chief product and technology officer Elizabeth Stone, Affleck revealed that he was worried about AI technology growing “outside of the ecosystem of filmmakers and artists.”
“I saw what I thought was a real opportunity and a real authentic danger,” Affleck said in the video. “But most importantly, I thought this is a really meaningful innovation.”
The actor and director go on to explain that InterPositive is a tool for filmmakers designed to connect them more to the process of filmmaking, using AI to build unique models based on a project’s film dailies.
“It’s not about text prompting or generating something from nothing,” Affleck explained. “You’re building a model from your own material. That’s how this works.”
“You have to create your movie, essentially, first before you can really build your model around your movie using AI,” he added. “And once you do that, you have your model. You control it.”

In a statement from Stone included in Thursday’s acquisition announcement, Netflix’s chief product and technology officer said that the streamer is teaming up with Affleck’s company because of their “shared belief that innovation should empower storytellers, not replace them.”
“InterPositive’s impressive technology is purpose-built for filmmakers and showrunners to work with tools that naturally support their creative visions and how they want to bring them to life,” Stone said.
Meanwhile, Affleck said in his written message that he “couldn’t be happier” to partner with Netflix and looks “forward to providing the broader creative community with access to what we build and the future we’re working towards together.”

Ben Affleck sells his artificial intelligence start-up to Netflix
Ben Affleck has sold his artificial intelligence start-up InterPositive to Netflix.
In a rare acquisition by the streaming company, the deal was completed after the actor, 53, founded the Los Angeles-based company in 2022 to develop AI-powered tools designed to assist filmmakers in the production and post-production process.
Netflix confirmed the purchase of InterPositive, although the terms of the buy-up have not been disclosed.
The company said the entire 16-person InterPositive team of engineers, researchers and creatives will join Netflix as part of the acquisition.
Ben will also serve as a senior adviser to Netflix, providing ongoing guidance on the development of the technology. Netflix said it intends to provide access to InterPositive’s tools to its creative partners rather than sell the technology commercially.
Speaking in a video shared by Netflix alongside the acquisition announcement, Ben said the technology is designed to support filmmakers rather than generate content automatically.
He added: “It’s not about text-prompting or generating something from nothing.
“AI, people mostly think of it as making something from nothing: ‘I’m gonna type something into a computer and it’s gonna give me a movie’. That’s not what this is.”
Ben explained InterPositive’s system works by building an AI model using footage from an existing production.
The model can then be introduced into post-production to assist with processes including colour mixing, relighting shots and adding visual effects.
According to Netflix, the tools were designed to place filmmakers at the centre of the creative process rather than replace them.
Netflix’s chief content officer Bela Bajaria said the technology would give filmmakers greater control over how their projects are completed.
She said in a statement: “Our relationship with artists has always been grounded in trust: supporting the full range of their creativity and ensuring they have the power to decide how their films and shows are made.”
Bela added: “We believe new tools should expand creative freedom, not constrain it or replace the work of writers, directors, actors and crews.
“Ben and his team at InterPositive are part of a long tradition in our industry of artists leading the way in how innovation is used in storytelling.
“Their work is about giving filmmakers more choices, more control and more protection for their vision. We’re excited to build on that legacy together, with creators and their artistic intentions at the centre of everything we do.”

Less than a week after dropping out of the bidding for Warner Bros Discovery, Netflix has made a smaller but intriguing acquisition of an AI firm founded by Ben Affleck.
InterPositive, which makes tools developed by and intended for filmmakers, had been in stealth mode prior to the transaction. As of Thursday, it is part of Netflix, with its 16 employees to be integrated into the broader workforce. Affleck will take on the role of senior advisor.
The deal builds on comments from management as AI has exploded onto the scene in the past few years, with executives stressing the ways it can improve quality rather than reducing costs or staffing. The company captured a proprietary data set on a closed soundstage, eventually leading to the company’s first model, which Affleck writes is “trained to understand visual logic and editorial consistency, while preserving cinematic rules under real-world production challenges such as missing shots, background replacements or incorrect lighting.”
In other words, the focus is on filmmaking technique, not the performance of the actors. The tool also allows directors or filmmakers to upload dailies to hone the model for a specific project.
Still, anything that touches on AI has become something of a third rail for Hollywood. That may be why Netflix also released a video discussion Thursday, featuring Affleck, Netflix chief product and technology officer Elizabeth Stone, and chief content officer Bela Bajaria discussing what role the tech may play in the creative process, and what InterPositive and Netflix do differently than the AI giants threatening to swallow the rest of the economy.

La compañía desarrolla herramientas basadas en IA diseñadas para optimizar procesos de producción de películas y series, un movimiento que refleja cómo Hollywood comienza a adoptar —con mayor pragmatismo— tecnologías que hace apenas unos años generaban fuertes tensiones laborales.
Diversos estudios sugieren que la IA podría transformar profundamente la economía del entretenimiento. Según explicó la directora de contenidos de Netflix, Bela Bajaria, la visión es clara: “Las nuevas herramientas deben ampliar la libertad creativa, no reemplazar el trabajo de escritores, directores o actores”.
IA de amenaza a herramienta creativa

La tecnología desarrollada por la empresa de Affleck se basa en un modelo entrenado para comprender la lógica visual del lenguaje cinematográfico, permitiendo resolver problemas comunes de rodaje como tomas faltantes, inconsistencias de iluminación o continuidad narrativa. ***
- Netflix confirmó que adquirirá InterPositive, startup creada por Ben Affleck en 2022 para herramientas de postproducción apoyadas por IA.
- La tecnología no busca crear actores sintéticos: se centra en continuidad, ajustes de iluminación y mejoras de entorno usando metraje de la propia producción.
- Affleck se incorporará como asesor senior y Netflix afirma que su enfoque es “empoderar a los narradores, no reemplazarlos”.

Netflix informó la mañana del jueves que está adquiriendo InterPositive, una empresa de tecnología cinematográfica fundada en 2022 por el actor Ben Affleck. Los términos financieros del acuerdo no fueron divulgados. Como parte del trato, el actor se unirá a la empresa como asesor senior.
La adquisición encaja con el enfoque que Netflix ha venido comunicando sobre el uso de IA generativa en cinematografía. La empresa ya ha utilizado IA generativa para efectos especiales en parte de su contenido original. Además, según ha señalado a inversionistas, considera que está “muy bien posicionada para aprovechar de manera efectiva los avances continuos en IA”.
En un mercado donde la IA está reconfigurando industrias creativas y tecnológicas, la decisión también puede leerse como una apuesta por integrar capacidades propietarias dentro del flujo de producción. En vez de depender solo de proveedores externos, Netflix suma un equipo y un modelo que, según la descripción pública, fue pensado para operar bajo reglas y necesidades típicas de un set y una sala de edición.
Para lectores familiarizados con el impacto de la IA en finanzas y mercados, la analogía es directa: así como los modelos automatizan tareas sin eliminar la supervisión humana en trading o análisis, en cine la promesa es acelerar tareas repetitivas sin quitar el control final a directores, editores y equipos creativos. Netflix insiste en esa narrativa de apoyo, no sustitución, en un contexto de debate global sobre automatización y empleo creativo.
Qué es InterPositive y por qué Ben Affleck la creó
Affleck explicó en un comunicado que empezó a pensar en cómo la IA impactaría el futuro de la cinematografía en 2022, año en que se fundó InterPositive. Afirmó que su objetivo era “preservar lo que hace humana la narración humana, que es el juicio”. También señaló que buscó “proteger el poder de la creatividad humana”.
El punto central del proyecto, de acuerdo con su planteamiento, es que la IA no reemplace la decisión artística. En cine, muchas elecciones no son puramente técnicas: la continuidad puede romperse a propósito, una luz puede ser imperfecta por estética, o un fondo puede mantenerse por intención narrativa. Esa frontera entre corrección técnica e intención creativa es donde, según Affleck, InterPositive intenta operar con restricciones y criterios.
Affleck remarcó que InterPositive no está tratando de crear actores de IA ni interpretaciones sintéticas. Esa aclaración es clave, porque una parte relevante de la conversación pública sobre IA en entretenimiento se concentra en “dobles” digitales y actuaciones generadas. En cambio, InterPositive se posiciona como una capa de asistencia para trabajar con material real ya filmado.
Según su descripción, la empresa creó un modelo que ayuda a los equipos de producción a trabajar con metraje de sus propias producciones. La meta es facilitar ediciones en la postproducción, como resolver problemas de continuidad o hacer ajustes de iluminación o mejoras al entorno. La propuesta apunta a una necesidad cotidiana: producir bajo presión, con tomas imperfectas y restricciones de tiempo, y luego “rescatar” el material sin regrabar.
Qué hace el modelo: lógica visual, consistencia editorial y reglas cinematográficas
Affleck describió el proceso como una ruta de investigación y desarrollo intensiva que llevó al “primer modelo” de InterPositive. En sus palabras, fue entrenado para entender la “lógica visual y la consistencia editorial”, mientras preserva reglas cinematográficas. También subrayó que el entrenamiento considera desafíos de producción del mundo real.
Entre esos desafíos, mencionó ejemplos concretos: tomas faltantes, reemplazos de fondos o iluminación incorrecta. En la práctica, son problemas habituales que aparecen cuando una escena se graba en distintos días, con cambios de clima, disponibilidad limitada de locaciones o ajustes de último minuto. Tradicionalmente, resolverlo implica trabajo manual detallado, nuevas filmaciones o concesiones creativas.
El planteamiento de InterPositive sugiere que su IA puede funcionar como una herramienta de apoyo para detectar o corregir esas inconsistencias, manteniendo la continuidad y la coherencia del montaje. Eso no elimina el rol humano, pero sí podría reducir el costo de iteración. Para una plataforma con escala global como Netflix, incluso pequeñas eficiencias por producción podrían acumularse en mejoras relevantes de tiempos y procesos.
La otra pieza es la noción de límites. Affleck afirmó que incorporaron “restricciones para proteger la intención creativa”, con el fin de diseñar herramientas para una exploración responsable. La idea, según lo expresado, es mantener las decisiones creativas en manos de los artistas y asegurar que los beneficios de la tecnología “fluyan directamente a la historia” que buscan contar.
Netflix: “empoderar a los narradores, no reemplazarlos”
Elizabeth Stone, directora de producto y tecnología de Netflix, sostuvo en un comunicado que la aproximación de la compañía a la IA “siempre se ha centrado en servir significativamente las necesidades de la comunidad creativa y de nuestros miembros”. En esa visión, la IA se usa como infraestructura de apoyo para mejorar el producto final y la experiencia del público, sin redefinir quién toma las decisiones artísticas.
Stone añadió que el equipo de InterPositive se une a Netflix debido a una creencia compartida: “la innovación debe empoderar a los narradores, no reemplazarlos”. El mensaje resulta relevante en un entorno donde creadores y sindicatos han expresado preocupaciones sobre sustitución laboral, uso de semejanza e incentivos para producir contenido con menos participación humana.
La compra también refuerza una línea ya mencionada por Netflix: la compañía ha usado IA generativa para efectos especiales en contenido original. La diferencia ahora es que se integra una firma fundada para construir modelos orientados a postproducción con reglas del lenguaje cinematográfico. Eso puede traducirse en herramientas internas, flujos de trabajo más estandarizados y una adopción más consistente dentro del estudio.
De acuerdo con TechCrunch, la adquisición se alinea con el enfoque de Netflix sobre IA generativa y con su mensaje a inversionistas de que está “muy bien posicionada” para capitalizar avances continuos. Aunque la nota no detalla montos, el movimiento sugiere una competencia por talento y propiedad intelectual, algo que también se observa en otras industrias tecnológicas cuando la IA se vuelve un diferenciador estratégico.
Implicaciones para la industria creativa y el debate sobre IA
InterPositive insiste en que su enfoque no se centra en “actores de IA”, y Netflix recalca el control creativo. Aun así, el anuncio se inserta en una discusión más amplia sobre cómo la IA redefine procesos, presupuestos y roles. En cine y series, la postproducción suele ser una de las áreas con mayor carga técnica y plazos ajustados, por lo que la automatización parcial puede cambiar la economía del sector.
Para audiencias interesadas en IA, mercados y tecnología, el caso ilustra una tendencia: las empresas buscan modelos especializados y verticales, entrenados para tareas concretas y con restricciones de uso. En vez de depender solo de herramientas generalistas, se construyen sistemas que respeten reglas del dominio, como continuidad visual, coherencia de edición y limitaciones de una producción real.

Netflix Acquires Ben Affleck’s AI Firm InterPositive
Netflix has confirmed a major new acquisition that signals a shift in how the streaming giant plans to use AI. On Thursday, the company announced it is buying InterPositive, a technology firm founded by Oscar-winning actor and director Ben Affleck.
Ben Affleck started the Los Angeles-based company in 2022 after watching how early AI models were being developed. Unlike many AI companies that focus on generating video from text, InterPositive creates tools designed to help professional filmmakers with the technical side of their craft.
As part of this deal, Affleck will join Netflix as a senior advisor. The entire InterPositive team, which includes fewer than twenty researchers, engineers, and creative experts, will also move over to Netflix.
While the financial details of the deal were not shared, the timing is interesting. It comes just a week after Netflix decided not to move forward with a massive bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery. Instead, the company seems to be focusing on building its own internal technology to make production more efficient.
It is important to understand that this technology is not meant to replace actors or writers. Instead, it focuses on “finishing” and “technical cleanup.” In simple terms, this means the AI helps fix small mistakes or adjustments that usually take a long time in post-production.
For example, the tools can help with continuity, which is making sure everything in a scene looks the same even if the shots were filmed hours or days apart. It can also adjust lighting or fix background elements that do not look quite right. InterPositive built its software by filming footage on a controlled soundstage to teach the AI how light and cameras work in the real world.
Netflix executives have been quick to point out that they want these tools to empower workers rather than replace them. This is a sensitive topic in Hollywood, especially after recent strikes where creative professionals expressed fear that AI might take their jobs.

Après avoir abandonné le rachat de Warner Bros, Netflix choisit un tout autre terrain d’acquisition : InterPositive, la société de technologie cinématographique fondée par Ben Affleck en 2022, spécialisée dans le développement d’outils d’intelligence artificielle conçus par et pour les cinéastes. L’intégralité de l’équipe rejoint Netflix et Ben Affleck prend le rôle de conseiller. Le montant du rachat n’a pas été divulgué.
Netflix se met un peu plus à l’intelligence artificielle
Netflix présente ce rapprochement comme une convergence de missions : utiliser la technologie émergente de façon à « protéger et élargir les choix créatifs », une philosophie que le groupe dit défendre depuis plus de 20 ans en associant la technologie et la création pour aider les films et les séries à trouver leur public.
Ben Affleck a fondé InterPositive en 2022 après avoir décidé d’explorer le secteur technologique. En collaboration avec des ingénieurs, chercheurs et cadres créatifs, il a constitué un ensemble de données propriétaires qui ont été capturées sur un plateau fermé, aboutissant au premier modèle de la société. Ce modèle est, selon Ben Affleck, « entraîné pour comprendre la logique visuelle et la cohérence éditoriale, tout en préservant les règles cinématographiques face aux défis de production réels tels que des plans manquants, des remplacements de décors ou un éclairage incorrect ».
L’approche est délibérément technique et non générative : l’outil IA ne touche pas à la performance des acteurs et ne prétend pas créer des films à partir d’un simple prompt, contrairement à des solutions comme Sora d’OpenAI qui ciblent des contenus courts. Il s’agit d’intervenir sur des segments précis de la production et de la post-production pour les accélérer et les simplifier, tout en laissant les créatifs aux commandes. Les réalisateurs peuvent par ailleurs importer leurs rushs quotidiens pour affiner le modèle sur un projet spécifique.
De possibles suppressions d’emplois à cause de l’IA
En rachetant InterPositive, Netflix revendique une approche « d’innovation portée par les créateurs » qui place le cinéaste au centre du processus, une philosophie assumée face aux outils qui cherchent à automatiser la création elle-même.
Cette nuance ne neutralise pas les enjeux sociaux pour l’industrie du cinéma à Hollywood. En automatisant certaines étapes de post-production, même de façon ciblée, ces outils IA menacent des emplois techniques au sein des équipes de tournage et de montage. Surtout, en se positionnant en leader sur ce terrain, Netflix risque d’entraîner l’ensemble du secteur dans la même direction : lorsque la première plateforme de streaming au monde s’engage dans cette voie, les autres studios ont historiquement tendance à suivre.

Netflix Acquires AI Company InterPositive Founded by Ben Affleck
March 5, 2026
Netflix has announced the acquisition of InterPositive, the filmmaking technology company founded by Ben Affleck that develops AI-powered tools built by and for filmmakers.
“InterPositive’s mission — to use emerging technology in ways that protect and expand creative choice — is deeply aligned with Netflix’s longstanding belief that innovation should serve storytellers and the creative process,” according to the announcement.
Affleck will join as senior advisor.
“[With the acquisition] we’re investing in creator-led innovation that keeps filmmakers at the center of the process,” Netflix announced.
“In 2022, I spent a lot of time observing the early rise of AI in production. As a filmmaker, I could see how these models came up short,” Affleck said in a statement. “For artists to apply these tools towards telling the stories we dedicate our lives to, they need to be purpose-built to represent and protect all the qualities that make a great story: the nuances of filmmaking, the predictable — and unpredictable — challenges of production environments, the distortion of a lens or the way light shape-shifts across a scene.
“We also need to preserve what makes storytelling human, which is judgment. The kind that takes decades to build, experience to hone and that only people can have. I knew I had a responsibility to my peers and our industry, to protect the power of human creativity and the people behind it. In creating InterPositive, I sought to do just that.
“Together with a small team of engineers, researchers and creatives, I began filming a proprietary dataset on a controlled soundstage with all the familiarities of a full production. I wanted to build a workflow that captures what happens on a set, with vocabulary that matched the language cinematographers and directors already spoke and included the kind of consistency and controls they would expect.
“Intensive research and development led to our first model, trained to understand visual logic and editorial consistency, while preserving cinematic rules under real-world production challenges such as missing shots, background replacements or incorrect lighting. We also built in restraints to protect creative intent, so the tools are designed for responsible exploration while keeping creative decisions in the hands of artists — and ensuring that the benefits of this technology flow directly back to the story they’re trying to tell.
“The results of this foundational work were deliberately smaller datasets and models focused on filmmaking techniques — rather than performances — creating tools that artists can use, control and benefit from.
“From the invention of the moving image to the transition to digital, from motion capture to virtual production, technology has evolved alongside the artists who use it. Our shared commitment to continuing this legacy makes joining together a natural next step, in addition to Netflix’s decades of experience applying and scaling technology responsibly. Our values, combined with our complementary strengths, will ensure these tools are used with the same care and responsibility with which they were built.
“I couldn’t be happier for this work to continue with the team at Netflix, and look forward to providing the broader creative community with access to what we build and the future we’re working towards together.”
“Our approach to AI has always been focused on meaningfully serving the needs of the creative community and our members,” Elizabeth Stone, Netflix chief product and technology officer, said in a statement. “The InterPositive team is joining Netflix because of our shared belief that innovation should empower storytellers, not replace them. InterPositive’s impressive technology is purpose-built for filmmakers and showrunners to work with tools that naturally support their creative visions and how they want to bring them to life. We’re excited to welcome the InterPositive team to Netflix and continue building towards a future of entertainment where technology plays a part in how stories are made, but people — and their ideas, craft and judgment — remain at the core of great storytelling.”
“Our relationship with artists has always been grounded in trust: supporting the full range of their creativity and ensuring they have the power to decide how their films and shows are made,” Bela Bajaria, Netflix chief content officer, said in a statement. “We believe new tools should expand creative freedom, not constrain it or replace the work of writers, directors, actors, and crews. Ben and his team at InterPositive are part of a long tradition in our industry of artists leading the way in how innovation is used in storytelling. Their work is about giving filmmakers more choices, more control and more protection for their vision. We’re excited to build on that legacy together, with creators and their artistic intentions at the center of everything we do.”
